messages.text: Will it pay for itself?

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. At 650 W it's about $34/month at 10¢, and you get a full draw at a 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes, for years.

What do you pay per kWh?
I wont be minig btc since you require 100000'ss of Terahas to even compete....10 cents 6pm to 8am , and 7 cents the rest
Ran the power-cost calculator · 8.2¢/kWh

Right — you're not out-hashing a farm. Two ways people run a 40T: pointed at a pool it pays small, steady sats to your own wallet, or solo where every block is a draw you get around the clock for years.

At your blend (~8¢) the power runs about $38 a month. $799, ships December 7, 2026.

Pool sats or lottery shot — which were you thinking?
?   I'll be mining whatever is profitabe.       the least congested pool..

Fair, but pool size doesn't change the payout much — you're paid on your share of the hashrate, not on congestion. Smaller pools just pay lumpier.

Where the 40T earns its keep is cost per TH: 40 TH at 650 W for $799 is the cheapest per terahash we sell. Want me to put one in a cart?
lol so your saying   1000 ppl on 40th miners instead of one or 2 wont affect it very badly?

Correct — in a pool more miners means the pool finds more blocks, and you still get paid your slice. 1,000 extra 40Ts in your pool doesn't shrink your cut.

What does move it is global network difficulty, and that's the same whichever pool you join.

Solo is the opposite: there you want the whole block or nothing.
oh, were talking about the same thing ... more miners = bigger hashrate :-)

Same thing, yes — network hashrate goes up, difficulty follows, everyone's slice gets thinner. That's the one number to watch, not the pool.

The 40T is the most TH per dollar we sell, at 650 W and about $38 a month on your rate. $799, ships December 7, 2026.

Want me to build the cart?
I've been doing pctechie crap 35 years    :-)....

Then you'll have this hashing in ten minutes — stratum URL, your wallet as the worker, done. No hand-holding needed.

Where would you run it? 650 W and a real fan, so it wants a garage or basement rather than a desk.
cart?      and yes I'm buying one  in 1 or 2 months, after that I'll be buying more
Searched the catalog · Magic Miner 40T
Built a cart

Cart's ready — one Magic Miner 40T, $799, Batch 8, ships December 7, 2026:

https://heliumdeploy.myshopify.com/cart/c/····

Worth knowing: batches sell out and each new one carries a later date, so buying now holds a December slot rather than a spring one.
:-)   you know they make $800 a day on a  (unamed coin?

I'll take your word on it — I won't quote altcoin earnings I can't verify.

What I can say: our SHA-256 units mine Bitcoin, and the scrypt side (DOGE/LTC merge-mined) is the Hammer DC06 and Nexus L1. If you want numbers on those, tell me which coin you mean and I'll stick to what we actually sell.
pfft   she256 calc on lesser coins everybody seems to ignore because of simple greed

True enough — low-difficulty SHA-256 chains have far fewer miners pointed at them.

The 40T doesn't care. It's a plain SHA-256 machine taking any stratum pool, so you point it at whatever chain you've done the math on and change it whenever you like.

Cart's live above whenever you're ready.
lol I 'm not greed, I'll be giving 70% away :-)    see ya it a bit.....    I'm disabled so,,,, take couple months for $800 :-)

Understood — saving up is a fine way to do it. Worth knowing the batches move: by then it'll likely be a later batch than December 7.

Before you go, one thing: when you come back in a couple of months, is it the 40T you'll be buying, or are you still weighing the smaller units?
yes
Got it — the 40T it is. See you in a couple of months, and good luck with the pool hunting.
the smaller unit are..... neet but useless given a thing callled  ANTminer :-(

Fair. A 6 TH Bitaxe next to an S21 is a toy — fine for learning, not for stacking.

The 40T is where it stops being a toy: same BM1370 chips the big boxes use, 16 J/TH, just thirty of them instead of a few hundred, and it runs in a room you live near.

See you in a couple of months.
ty   i'll get a camera to bring truth to that lol

Do it — a dB meter app next to it makes a better video than the spec sheet does.

Take care, and come find me when you're ready to order.
dont care I've very hard of hearing. aand deaf on the leaf so

Then noise is one less thing to plan around — put it wherever the power and the airflow are good.

Heat still matters though: 650 W all day warms a small room. Enjoy it, and see you when you're ready.
:-)     well my gekko 70 giga hash usb one's are on 4 box fans so.. I go overboard on cooling...  wanna see a ryzen9 5950x never make it to 50 degrees  ? LOL

A 5950X under 50 is proper airflow, not luck. Box fans on Gekko sticks tells me the 40T will be the coolest-running one anybody owns.

It's got a dual fan and heatsink of its own, so yours will just be gravy. See you in a couple of months.
nono at full use it should creep past 90 :-(      thats why the co2 heatsink :-)  I'ma  it doesant exist I'll build one guy..

Ha — a build-it guy. One caution before you get ideas on the 40T: cracking it open or running it past stock voids the warranty, so keep the cooling external to the case and you're fine.

Stock it's ~650 W with its own dual fan. Plenty of room to overbuild around it.
oh ps and the first to break the moores's law at 10.2 ghz stable

10.2 stable would be a record worth filming.

Just know the ASIC side doesn't clock like a CPU — the 40T's Turbo mode is 50 TH at 850 W and it voids the warranty, so I'd run it stock and point the tinkering at the cooling.

Cart's saved. See you when you're ready.
650 watts?

Yes, 650 W at the wall in Standard, 40 TH/s. Three modes: Eco 30 TH at 450 W, Standard 40 TH at 650 W, Turbo 50 TH at 850 W.

Built-in 1,400 W PSU, IEC C14, 100–240 V. Normal wall outlet, about $38 a month at your rate.
my rate?  oh crap I fergot its natural gas....   we have generac, so 0 cents :_)

Not zero — the gas still meters. A Generac running a 650 W load 24/7 burns fuel for it, so work out your cost per therm and you'll have the real rate.

The good news is it's a steady, small load, and whatever that number is, it's yours to pour into the machine instead of the grid's.
I'm already sold... :-)
